package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://malicious.example.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential files are read and exfiltrated to an external server controlled by the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and send their contents via HTTPS POST to an external domain.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that accesses ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and performs network requests to external domains
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to https://malicious.example.com/upload during package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations that trigger network connections to https://malicious.example.com/upload or similar domains during setup.py execution. Flag any package that reads sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and attempts to exfiltrate their contents over the network. Automated scanning of setup.py for file access patterns and outbound requests to untrusted domains can be used to detect this behavior.
